ALESSANDRO DE STEFANI, ELO´ISA GRIFO, AND JACK JEFFRIES
Abstract. We characterize symbolic powers of prime ideals in polynomial rings over any
ﬁeld in terms of Z-linear diﬀerential operators, and of prime ideals in polynomial rings
over complete discrete valuation rings with a p-derivation δ in terms of Z-linear diﬀerential
operators and of δ. This extends previous work of the same authors, as it allows the removal
of separability hypotheses that were otherwise necessary. The absence of separability and
the fact that modules of Z-linear diﬀerential operators are typically not ﬁnitely generated
require the introduction of new techniques. As a byproduct, we extend a characterization
of symbolic powers due to Cid-Ruiz which also holds in the nonsmooth case. Finally, we
produce an example of an unramiﬁed discrete valuation ring that has no p-derivations.

2.1. Symbolic powers. Let R be a commutative ring with unity, and I be an ideal in R.
Let W be the complement in R of the minimal primes of I. For n ⩾1, the nth symbolic

i.e., with the Q-primary component of Qn.
A classical theorem of Zariski and Nagata [Zar49, Nag62] identiﬁes the nth symbolic
power of a prime Q ⊆C[x1, . . . , xd] as the ideal of all functions that vanish up to order n

The main results are Theorems A and B, which establish that the nth (mixed) diﬀerential
power of a prime ideal Q in a polynomial ring over any ﬁeld is equal to the nth symbolic
power. In particular, for a polynomial ring over a perfect ﬁeld, the result follows from the
Zariski-Nagata theorem, which states that Q(n) = Q⟨n⟩K, where Q⟨n⟩K is the K-linear
diﬀerential power. However, when the ﬁeld is not perfect, we need to consider Z-linear diﬀerential
operators instead, which leads us to Theorem A.

Similarly, for prime ideals containing p in a polynomial ring over a complete unramiﬁed
discrete valuation ring, we need to consider mixed diﬀerential powers involving both the Z-linear
and p-derivation operators, which is the content of Theorem B.

The paper also includes a discussion of Brenner, the third author, and N´u˜nez Betancourt’s
result [BJNB19], which shows that in singular rings, symbolic powers cannot always be
described by diﬀerential operators. However, the authors here improve upon that by showing
that for singular rings, one can sometimes use diﬀerential operators to describe symbolic powers,
but not in full generality.

Furthermore, the paper generalizes Cid-Ruiz’s [CR21] result by removing the need for
separability assumptions, which was a key part of his approach using Z-linear diﬀerential operators.

The authors also provide an example of an unramiﬁed discrete valuation ring that does not
have a p-derivation, which shows that the completeness condition on the ring is necessary for
Theorem B.

In summary, the paper establishes that the nth symbolic power of a prime ideal can be
described using Z-linear diﬀerential operators in the equicharacteristic case, and using mixed
diﬀerential powers involving both Z-linear and p-derivation operators in the mixed characteristic
case. These results remove the separability assumptions required in previous work and extend
the applicability of the Zariski-Nagata theorem to more general settings.
